label: second copy step (output orig token 1) in long sequences (L>=8)
explanation: Fires almost only at the copy step right after <DEL> (t = L+1, input = fed-back first token, output = original token 1); 99.9% of activation mass is at recall_idx == 1. Silent in the original phase, at the delimiter, and at every later copy step. Strongly gated by length: none for L<=5, rare at L=6, ~1% of L=7 steps, ~38%/50% firing rate at L=8/9 recall_idx 1, and mass grows with L (L=9 carries 56%). Within those steps it fires on about half; token identity modulates rate and magnitude: higher when the fed-back first token is m/z/e/3, the output token (orig 1) is u/2/k/w/t, or the next output (orig 2) is 2/u/k/p/o. Top activations (~3.0) are L=8-9 sequences starting m or z followed by u/2/k. Adding those token lists raises dev F1 from 0.59 to 0.70, but the lists are ad hoc, so the simple position+length predicate is recorded.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the second original token (most: u, k, 2, w, t, v; least: 1, l, z, f) and the third original token (most: u, 2, k, p, o, i; least: x, f, s, z); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=8 & t=9, L=9 & t=10.
